label: Quotient Social Post
description: Quotient social post editor/preview showing a LinkedIn-style published post with author info, rich text content, embedded media card, engagement actions, and status bar. Supports animated entrance and optional scripted interactions.

post_text.label: Post Body Text (use \n\n for paragraph breaks)
post_text.default:
This week's running story has been about companies blowing past their AI budgets with insane token bills. I heard one about a guy who accidentally racked up a $500k Claude bill.

I have no idea if that's true — it probably isn't — and I think most of these stories are totally overblown. At Quotient, we're some of the most hardcore AI users on the planet and we rarely spend more than a few thousand bucks per person on tokens each month.

That said, I was a little surprised when I saw a $2,000 Quotient bill last month. Yes, we pay for our own software. It's called eating your own dogfood. Maybe you've heard of it. And apparently we were using it a LOT, because we blew straight through our plan's token allotment.

Not exactly a $500k nightmare. But still — a surprise.

So we immediately shipped spending caps and usage notifications, so our customers never have surprise bills.

These kinds of controls are going to be crucial now that software is evolving past the seat-based model. Every company is going to spend more and more on tokens in the future, and I think that's money well spent. We just need to make sure the controls are in place — so nobody ends up like the guy who almost bankrupted his company with a Claude bill.
